items.name: Incident report / postmortem write-up
items.one_line: The written record after an outage, security event or project failure: what happened, who and what was affected, why, how it was fixed and detected, and owned actions so it does not recur.
items.value_evidence: Written in-house by engineers and on-call teams (Google SRE book; PagerDuty's guide is aimed at on-call practitioners and managers); no freelance market category was searched or found, so paid writing demand is assumed small.

sources.title: Google SRE book, ch. 15 'Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure'
sources.supports: 'A postmortem is a written record of an incident, its impact, the actions taken ..., the root cause(s), and the follow-up actions ...'; blameless; triggers such as user-visible downtime, data loss, on-call intervention, monitoring failure

sources.title: Google SRE book: Example postmortem
sources.supports: a complete worked example with Summary, Impact, Root Causes, Trigger, Resolution, Detection, Action Items, Lessons Learned, Timeline

sources.title: PagerDuty Postmortem Documentation
sources.supports: 'a successful postmortem process is based on a culture of honesty, learning, and accountability'; blameless postmortems; audience is on-call practitioners and managers

items.note: Structure: fw:postmortem_blameless. Two audiences: the internal version (full technical detail, timeline, action items with owners) and an optional customer-facing summary (plain language, impact window, what changed, no internal names); the live outage notice is genre:crisis_statement. Tone: factual, past tense, blameless; times in one zone. In India, a cyber incident may also need reporting to CERT-In; check the current CERT-In directions before writing any public statement (not researched here).

items.name: Influencer media kit / rate card
items.one_line: A short document a creator sends brands: who they are, audience size and demographics, engagement, past collaborations and results, collaboration options and (optionally) rates.
items.value_evidence: Sold as a gig on Fiverr (e.g. 'design an influencer media kit template' at $35, seen in a 2026-10-05 search) and covered by creator-platform guides (Later 2025, Influencer Marketing Hub 2024); usually bundled with design, no separate writing category found.

sources.title: Later (Nikki Canning, updated 2025-06-04): How to Make a Media Kit for Influencers
sources.supports: 'Think of your influencer media kit as your business card, CV, and portfolio of work all in one document'; sections: bio, social stats, audience demographics, blog or website, previous partnerships and testimonials

sources.title: Influencer Marketing Hub (2024-09-02): How to Create an Influencer Media Kit
sources.supports: definition: 'a document that showcases an influencer's skills, audience, and previous collaborations to potential brand partners'; sections end with suggested collaboration options and pricing rates; whether to print rates is 'a polarizing point'; 'Keep your media kit brief; ideally, limit it to three pages'

sources.title: Fiverr gig: influencer media kit template
sources.supports: media kits are bought as a freelance deliverable (demand signal only)

items.note: Not the corporate press kit (genre:press_kit). Every number must come from the platform's own insights on a stated date (followers, reach, engagement, audience split by city/age/gender); rounding up or using bought followers is a misrepresentation to the brand. Rate card lines are per deliverable (reel, story set, static post, YouTube integration) plus usage rights, exclusivity and whitelisting/boosting as separate lines. Indian brands will ask for ASCI disclosure compliance (comp:asci_influencer): state that paid posts carry the label. Bilingual or Hinglish creators should state language mix of the audience.
